papers.title_in_file: Ultra-bright Quantum Photon Sources on Chip
papers.version_note: arXiv:2010.04242v1 [physics.optics] 8 Oct 2020; the Supplementary Materials it refers to are not in the text.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental paper reporting photon-pair and heralded single-photon generation in a Z-cut periodically poled lithium niobate microring with MHz-scale rates at microwatt pump powers.

assertions.value: The authors describe the device as a triply resonant, Z-cut periodically-poled lithium niobate (PPLN) microring resonator whose light waves are in the low-loss fundamental modes and use the largest nonlinear susceptibility tensor element of lithium niobate.
quotes: It is a triply resonant, Z-cut periodically-poled lithium niobate (PPLN) microring resonator, where the light waves are all in the low-loss fundamental modes, with nearly perfect overlap,
and interact through LN’s largest nonlinear susceptibility tensor element (d33 ∼27 pm/V).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own device or apparatus setup.

assertions.value: The authors report a concentric poled region with a period of 3.85 µm, and a microring with a top width of 1.6 µm and a radius of 55 µm, fabricated on a Z-cut lithium niobate on insulator wafer with a 700-nm thick lithium niobate film on a 2-µm silicon dioxide layer.
quotes: a concentric periodically poled region is created with a period of 3.85 µm
microring structure with a top width of 1.6 µm and a radius of 55 µm
with a 700-nm thick LN thin ﬁlm bonded on 2-µm silicon dioxide layer above a silicon substrate
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own device or apparatus setup.

assertions.value: The authors report a shallow etch of 430 nm with 270 nm remaining and a sidewall angle of 70 degrees, and a pulley coupling waveguide with top width 300 nm and gap 500 nm designed for coupling of 90% (infrared) and 75% (visible).
quotes: (430 nm ethed, 270 nm remained) with 70◦ sidewall angle
A pulley waveguide (topwidth 300 nm, gap 500 nm, see Fig. 1(a))
good coupling for both IR (90%) and visible light (75%)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own device or apparatus setup.

assertions.value: The authors report loaded and intrinsic quality factors of about 1.0 and 2.6 (infrared mode) and about 1.5 and 2.3 (visible mode), each multiplied by ten to the fifth power (printed flat in the text layer).
assertions.anchor: Device Design and Fabrication, p.2; Fig. 1(b),(c)
quotes: We obtain QL(Q0) ≈ 1.0(2.6) × 105 (IR mode) and QL(Q0) ≈ 1.5(2.3) × 105 (visible mode)

assertions.value: The authors give the effective Hamiltonian of non-degenerate spontaneous parametric down-conversion in a single-mode cavity, with g the nonlinear coupling coeﬃcient between pump and photon pairs, a function of mode volume, spatial overlap, nonlinear susceptibility and phase matching.
assertions.anchor: Device Design and Fabrication, Eq. (1), p.1
quotes: In a singlemode cavity, the eﬀective Hamiltonian describing nondegenerate spontaneous parametric downconversion is:
g is the nonlinear coupling coeﬃcient between pump and photon pairs, which is a function of each’s mode volume, their spatial overlap, nonlinear susceptibility, and phase matching
assertions.certainty_reason: Eq. (1) and the definition of g are stated in the Device Design and Fabrication section.

assertions.value: The authors give the total photon pair generation rate as a function of g, the cavity dissipation rates and the pump power, for the phase matched case with no cavity detuning, and cite reference 19 for it. The text layer garbles the formula (equation two).
quotes: Assuming phase matched case and no cavity detuning, the total photon pair generation rate (PGR) is given by [19]:
where κj,o = ω/Qj,o are the cavity dissipation rates with j = s, i, p for the signal, idler, and pump modes
assertions.reader_inference: The formula itself is not recoverable from the text layer; only its conditions and the symbol definitions can be quoted.

assertions.value: The authors state that quasi-phase matching is the key to maximizing g, and that concentric periodic poling on the microring gives the strongest interaction between the fundamental quasi-TM modes at infrared (signal and idler) and visible (pump) wavelengths with ideal mode overlap.
quotes: The key to maximize the nonlinear coupling coeﬃcient g is quasi-phase matching.
while achieving ideal mode overlapping and utilizing the largest nonlinear tensor d33 in LN

assertions.value: The authors report fiber-chip-fiber coupling losses measured to be 11.5 dB around 1554 nm and 17.5 dB around 777 nm.
quotes: whose losses are measured to be 11.5 dB around 1554 nm and 17.5 dB around 777 nm
assertions.reader_inference: The text does not say how the on-chip pump powers quoted elsewhere are derived from fiber powers; these losses are the likely basis.

assertions.value: The authors report quasi-phase matched second-harmonic generation for resonance modes at 1554.6 nm and 777.3 nm at a temperature of 44.6 degrees Celsius.
quotes: a quasiphase matched SHG is achieved for optimal resonance modes at 1554.6 nm and its second-harmonic (SH) at 777.3 nm at 44.6 ◦C

assertions.value: The authors report that with 83 µW pump power in the input fiber, 80 nW of second-harmonic power is collected in the output fiber, and that accounting for coupling loss the normalized SHG efficiency (second-harmonic power over pump power squared) is estimated to be 122, 000%/W.
quotes: With 83 µW pump power in the input ﬁber, 80 nW SH power is collected in the output ﬁber.
the normalized SHG eﬃciency ηSHG = Psh/Pp2 is estimated to be 122, 000%/W

assertions.value: The authors report a single-photon nonlinearity of about 1.9 times ten to the minus six, computed from the normalized SHG efficiency, and later describe it as a giant single photon nonlinearity of about ten to the minus six.
assertions.anchor: Second-Harmonic Generation, p.2; Pair Generation Rate and Brightness, p.3
quotes: corresponding to single-photon nonlinearity ηphoton = ηSHG ωp2/Qp,t ≈ 1.9 × 10−6
facilitated by the giant single photon nonlinearity (∼ 10−6)

assertions.value: The authors report a temperature tolerance of 1.3 degrees Celsius for the SHG efficiency of the optimized cavity mode, from a Lorentzian fit.
quotes: showing a tolerance of 1.3◦C
with Lorentzianﬁtted temperature bandwidth at 1.3 ◦C

assertions.value: The authors report that the absolute SHG efficiency saturates at 20% with 350 µW on-chip pump power, and state that this indicates good thermal stability and a slightly over-coupled pump mode.
quotes: saturating at 20% with 350 µW on-chip pump power
indicate good thermal stability and slightly over-coupled condition for the pump mode
assertions.reader_inference: The thermal-stability and over-coupling statements are the authors' interpretation of the 20% saturation; no separate measurement of either is shown in the text.

assertions.value: The authors describe pumping the quasi-TM visible mode at the phase matched SHG wavelength (777.3 nm), long-pass filters with over 80 dB extinction, DWDM filters with 0.8 nm full width at half maximum, and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors with dark-count rate of 50-100 Hz and detection efficiency of 85%.
quotes: is excited for optimum photon-pair generation
(777.3 nm) is excited
free-space longpass ﬁlters with over 80 dB extinction ratio
narrow full width at half maximum (FWHM) transmission bandwidth of 0.8 nm
The SNSPDs have dark-count rate of 50-100 Hz and detection eﬃciency of 85%.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own device or apparatus setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the temporal resolution of the entire system is about 46 ps and that, after all insertion loss, chip-fiber coupling loss and detection efficiency, the signal and idler channel each has about 10 dB total loss.
quotes: the temporal resolution of the entire system in determining the arrival time of photon is about 46 ps
signal and idler channel each has about 10 dB total loss
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own device or apparatus setup.

assertions.value: The authors calculate the pair generation rate as N1N2/N12 from the signal rate N1, idler rate N2 and two-photon coincidence rate N12, with signal at 1545.8 nm and idler at 1563.5 nm, and define brightness B as the pair generation rate over on-chip pump power.
assertions.anchor: Pair Generation Rate and Brightness, p.3
quotes: PGR is simply calculated as N1N2/N12
the latter at 1545.8 nm and 1563.5 nm, respectively
deﬁned as PGR over on-chip pump power (B = PGR/Pp)
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as the paper's own method and definition in the Pair Generation Rate and Brightness section.

assertions.value: The authors report a measured brightness of 2.7 MHz per microwatt, inferred from the fitted slope of pair generation rate against on-chip pump power.
assertions.anchor: Pair Generation Rate and Brightness, p.3; Fig. 3(a)
quotes: is measured to be 2.7 MHz µW −1, as inferred from the ﬁtted slope of the data in Fig.3 (a)

assertions.value: The authors report that the observed brightness is about 2.6 times lower than the theoretical prediction of 7.0 MHz per microwatt, which they attribute mainly to extreme sensitivity to slight deviation from the ideal triply resonant condition.
assertions.anchor: Pair Generation Rate and Brightness, p.3
quotes: The observed brightness is about 2.6 times lower than the theoretical prediction of 7.0 MHz µW −1, mainly due to its extreme sensitivity in the slight deviation from the ideal triply resonant condition.
assertions.reader_inference: A stated limitation: the device does not reach its own predicted brightness. The attribution to detuning is the authors' claim; no detuning measurement is shown in the text.

assertions.value: The authors report photon-pair generation at 8.5 MHz and 36.3 MHz using 3.4 µW and 13.4 µW pump power respectively, with a coincidence to accidental ratio well above 100 at those rates.
quotes: we demonstrate photon-pair generation at high rates of 8.5 MHz and 36.3 MHz using only 3.4-µW and 13.4-µW pump power, respectively
The measured coincidence to accidental ratio is well above 100 at those high rates
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract says well above 100, while Table I lists 451 for the first row and >100 for the second.

assertions.value: The authors' Table I lists two rows for this work, both marked as spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources, with on-chip pump power 3.4 µW and 13.4 µW, pair generation rate 8.5 MHz and 36.3 MHz, rate at 1 µW of 2.53 MHz and 2.7 MHz, CAR of 451 and >100, and heralded auto-correlation 0.008 and 0.097. The text layer flattens the table; the pairing is by column order.
quotes: PGR 855 kHz 1.2 kHz 1.1 MHz 16 kHz 1 MHz 4.8 kHz 450 kHz 0.5 Hz 11 MHz 8.5 MHz 36.3 MHz
26.95 kHz 0.004 Hz 5.8 kHz 2.53 MHz 2.7 MHz
assertions.reader_inference: Row mapping is by column order in a flattened table; the rate at 1 µW values 2.53 MHz and 2.7 MHz match 8.5 MHz over 3.4 µW and 36.3 MHz over 13.4 µW.

assertions.value: The authors' Table I lists, for the prior silicon, silicon nitride, lithium niobate and aluminum nitride microcavity sources, a pair generation rate at 1 µW of 137 Hz, 8.3 Hz, 316 Hz, 292 Hz, 4 Hz, 2.27 Hz, 26.95 kHz, 0.004 Hz and 5.8 kHz, as cited from other work.
quotes: PGR @ 1µW 137 Hz 8.3 Hz 316 Hz 292 Hz 4 Hz 2.27 Hz
26.95 kHz 0.004 Hz 5.8 kHz 2.53 MHz 2.7 MHz
assertions.reader_inference: The largest prior entry is 26.95 kHz (the lithium niobate micro-disk row by column order); 2.7 MHz divided by 26.95 kHz is about 100, consistent with the paper's '100 times or more' claim. Prior-art rates are normalized by the authors to 1 µW and not independently checked.

assertions.value: The authors state that the efficiency corresponds to 100 times or more improvement over the state of the art across all existing material platforms, and that the brightness and pair generation rate are several orders of magnitude higher than previous microcavity pair sources.
assertions.anchor: Introduction, p.1; Pair Generation Rate and Brightness, p.3
quotes: This ultrahigh eﬃciency corresponds to 100 times or more improvement over the state of the art across all existing material platforms (see Table I).
the brightness and PGR of our PPLN microring photon pair source are several orders magnitude higher compared to the previously demonstrated state-
assertions.reader_inference: 'Several orders of magnitude' (p.3) is stronger than the roughly two orders of magnitude that Table I supports for rate per microwatt; for the raw pair rate 36.3 MHz against 11 MHz is about 3 times.

assertions.value: The authors state that the brightness and pair generation rate are facilitated by the giant single photon nonlinearity, an excellent single-mode condition, and the pure SPDC process in this system.
assertions.anchor: Pair Generation Rate and Brightness, p.3
quotes: The unmatched brightness and PGR observed in this work is facilitated by the giant single photon nonlinearity (∼ 10−6), an excellent single-mode condition, and the pure SPDC process in this system.

assertions.value: The authors define the coincidence to accidental ratio as (NCO/NAC) minus 1 with NCO the coincidence counts and NAC the accidental coincidence counts, and use a coincidence window of 200 ps given a cavity lifetime of about 80 ps.
quotes: The CAR is calculated as (NCO/NAC ) − 1, where NCO and NAC are deﬁned as coincidence and accidental coincidence counts, respectively.
Considering the cavity lifetime (τc ≈ 80 ps), we choose the coincidence window to be 200 ps
assertions.certainty_reason: The CAR definition and window are the paper's stated method.

assertions.value: The authors report a highest observed CAR of 14682±4427, from raw coincidence and accidental counts without accidental subtraction, at 210 nW on-chip pump power.
quotes: The highest observed CAR is 14682±4427 with raw coincidence and accidental counts, i.e., without accidental subtraction, measured with 210 nW on-chip pump power.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract and introduction quote this CAR; Table I lists 451 for the 3.4 µW row, so the two values are at different pump powers. The uncertainty is about 30% of the value.

assertions.value: The authors report a CAR of 205 ± 3 at a detected photon flux of 0.9 MHz.
quotes: a high CAR of 205 ± 3 can be achieved at detected photon ﬂux of 0.9 MHz

assertions.value: The authors state that the CAR is primarily limited by multi-photon emission, that it decreases exponentially with increasing on-chip pump power, and that this is a well-known trade-off for probabilistic photon sources.
quotes: the CAR are primarily limited by multi-photon emission

Evidently, CAR decreasing exponentially with increasing pump power on chip, a well-known trade-oﬀ between a high mean photon probability and unwanted multiphoton noise of any probabilistic photon source.
assertions.reader_inference: A stated limit on pump power versus purity. The exponential form is asserted from Fig. 3(b); no fit is described in the text.

assertions.value: The authors report CAR measured over five more channel pairs, and values varying from 500 to 1000 at an on-chip pump power of 1.7 µW; details are in Supplementary Materials, which are not in the text.
quotes: we have measured the CAR over ﬁve more channel pairs (see Supplementary Materials)
At a onchip pump power of 1.7 µW , the CAR values for those channels vary from 500 to 1000
assertions.reader_inference: Per-channel data are in the Supplementary Materials, not read here.

assertions.value: The authors describe heralding with signal photons at 1545.8 nm for idler photons at 1563.5 nm split by a splitter described as 50/50, a 200 ps timing window, a total counting period of 300 seconds, and a heralded auto-correlation computed as N123N1/N12N13 and then normalized.
quotes: We use the signal photons at 1545.8 nm for heralding single photons at the paired idler wavelength of 1563.5 nm.
The idler photons are split by a 50/50 splitter (∼ 1 dB IL) to Idler 1 and Idler 2 beams
The timing window is 200 ps for all measurements, and each total counting period is 300 seconds.
gH(2)(τ ) is calculated as N123N1/N12N13 and then normalized.
assertions.certainty_reason: The method and the formula are stated in the Heralded Single-Photon Generation section.

assertions.value: The authors report a best heralded auto-correlation at zero delay of 0.007 ± 0.0016, with Poissonian uncertainty, at a detected count rate of 250 kHz.
quotes: the best auto-correlation value at zero delay is measured to be gH(2)(0) = 0.007 ± 0.0016
250 kHz. Such a low auto-correlation points to the high ﬁdelity with very low noise of the heralded single photon state.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract, introduction and Fig. 3(d) caption give 0.008 as the headline value; the body gives 0.007 as the best. The difference lies within the quoted uncertainties and the text does not reconcile them.

assertions.value: The authors report, in the Fig. 3(d) caption, an anti-bunching dip with heralded auto-correlation at zero delay of 0.008 ± 0.0007 at 3.4 µW on-chip power, with all error bars estimated by Poissonian photon counting statistics.
quotes: anti-bunching dip of gH(2)(0) = 0.008 ± 0.0007 at 3.4 µW on-chip power
All error bars are estimated by Poissonian photon counting statistics.

assertions.value: The authors report that at a higher pump power the heralded auto-correlation remains at 0.097 ± 0.0076 with a detected photon rate of 2 MHz.
quotes: At a higher pump power, the auto-correlation remains at gH(2) = 0.097 ± 0.0076 even when the detected photon rate of N1 = 2 MHz.

assertions.value: The authors report a second non-degenerate pair (signal 1551.7 nm and idler 1557.6 nm) with heralded auto-correlation at zero delay of 0.005 ± 0.0009 at a detected count rate of 225 kHz; details are in Supplementary Materials, which are not in the text.
quotes: another non-degenerate pairs (signal-1551.7 nm and idler1557.6 nm) (see Supplementary Materials) also recorded impressively low gH2 (0) = 0.005 ± 0.0009 with detected count rate of N1 = 225 kHz

assertions.value: The authors state in the abstract that the same chip enables heralded single-photon generation at tens of megahertz rates, with auto-correlation 0.008 and 0.097 for the microwatt pumps.
quotes: The same chip enables heralded single-photon generation at tens of megahertz rates, each with low auto-correlation gH(2)(0) = 0.008 and 0.097 for the microwatt pumps.
observing a 8.5 MHz rate and 0.008 auto-correlation
assertions.reader_inference: The heralded measurements in the body report detected signal rates of 250 kHz, 2 MHz and 225 kHz; the megahertz-scale rates are the generated pair rates from Table I, corrected for about 10 dB loss per channel, not directly detected heralded single-photon rates.

assertions.value: The authors claim to present the first quantum circuit in lithium niobate on insulator that overcomes all shortcomings and approaches the ideal performance promised by the material.
quotes: Here, we present the ﬁrst quantum circuit in LNOI that overcomes all shortcomings and approaches the ideal performance promised by the material.

assertions.value: The authors state that the CAR notes the ultrahigh purity of the photon-pair states with perfect correlation and nearly zero noise, and in the conclusion that the photons are in pure quantum states owing to the nearly perfect single mode condition and the absence of background optical processes.
quotes: which notes the ultrahigh purity of the photon-pair states with perfect correlation, and with nearly zero noise
Thanks to the nearly perfect single mode condition and absence of background optical processes, those photons are in pure quantum states.
assertions.reader_inference: The text shows no purity measurement (such as a joint spectrum or interference visibility); the evidence offered is the CAR and the heralded auto-correlation, which test photon-number statistics, not state purity. A finite CAR also contradicts 'perfect correlation'.

assertions.value: The authors state that second-order nonlinear devices have orders of magnitude stronger nonlinear optical effects than third-order devices and are not subject to undesirable side third-order processes; and cite d31 of about 4.7 pm/V in lithium niobate and 4-6 pm/V in aluminum nitride as suboptimal susceptibilities of earlier circuits.
quotes: χ(2)-based devices enjoy orders of magnitude stronger nonlinear optical eﬀects while not subjet to undesirable side χ(3) processes
(e.g., d31 ∼4.7 pm/V in LN [17] and 4–6 pm/V in AIN [19])

assertions.value: The authors conclude that photons are created over multiple wavelength channels simultaneously, suiting high-dimensional entangled states and optical quantum logic, and that the circuits are ready to be integrated with electro-optical modulators and frequency converters on the same chip.
quotes: we show that such high-quality single and correlated photons are created over multiple wavelength channels simultaneously
the demonstrated quantum circuits are ready to be integrated with other optical elements, such as electro-optical modulators and frequency converters, on the same LNOI chip
assertions.reader_inference: No entanglement or integration with other elements is demonstrated in the text; these are stated prospects.
